images.title: Populations on a powers of 10 line
images.purpose: Places elephants, starlings, people and mosquitoes on one line marked in powers of 10.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long horizontal line with evenly spaced ticks for powers of 10 and four markers.
images.exact_structure: One long horizontal line in dark outline with 11 evenly spaced ticks for 10⁵, 10⁶ and so on up to 10¹⁵; only the first tick is labelled 10⁵ and the tenth tick 10¹⁴. Four markers with labels above: a teal (#0072B2) dot just past the 10⁵ tick (about 0.6 of the way to 10⁶) labelled elephants 4 × 10⁵; an amber (#E69F00) dot just past the 10⁹ tick labelled starlings 1.3 × 10⁹; a second amber dot just before the 10¹⁰ tick labelled people 8.2 × 10⁹; a reddish purple (#CC79A7) dot right at the 10¹⁴ tick labelled mosquitoes 1.1 × 10¹⁴. Stagger the starlings and people labels at two heights so they do not overlap. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Writing populations as powers of 10 lets us compare them by the exponent.
